subject: Friday's front page ran on stories that were days old
summary: A giant IPO, an AI-driven hacking warning, a broken bridge and an airline glitch all kept readers busy on a day with little new to say.

lead.head: The IPO everyone is waiting on
text: The biggest story of the day was money, and it was not new. Reports say Anthropic is set to price its IPO on Wednesday and start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday. The range runs from {low} to {high} a share, and the top of it puts the company at {valuation}.

The post that carried it drew the most readers by far, and it came from a prediction market, not a newsroom. That tells you who is paying attention to this listing. People who trade on outcomes want the number before the filing is in their inbox.

A valuation that size is a bet on how much AI work companies will pay for, and for how long. The price range is a guess about the answer. The first day of trading will start to replace it with a real one.

notes.head: The FBI says AI is speeding up break-ins
notes.text: The FBI warns that criminals and state-aligned hackers are using an open-source tool called ARTEX. It lets an AI model run the steps of an intrusion, which cuts the labor out of the attack. The bureau's own post is what spread. The practical change is that skill matters less and patience matters less, so defenders get less warning.

notes.head: Two claims about one bridge
notes.text: Ukraine says it destroyed the road span of the Kerch Bridge, Russia's main land link to occupied Crimea. Moscow says it will rebuild. Zelensky describes the strike as one stage of a longer operation. Both sides have said what they want believed, and repair crews will settle which statement ages better.

notes.head: United says it fixed its outage
notes.text: United Airlines reported a system outage that delayed departures for about an hour and a half. It came days after the nationwide FAA ground stop. United says the problem is fixed and has not named a cause, and reports say it did not look like a cyber issue.

text: Friday's pattern is that attention outran news. The stories readers picked were days old, and they stayed on top because nothing newer beat them.
My call is that the IPO is the one to watch, because it is the only one with a date on it. The rest are waiting on causes that nobody has given.

low.of: the bottom of the reported price range per share

high.of: the top of the reported price range per share

valuation.of: the reported valuation at the top of the range
